pr_title: Bluetooth: Controller: Fix headroom reservation for ISO
pr_body:
Calling `net_buf_reserve` removed any previous reservation, which includes the reservation by hci_ipc to hold the H4 type byte. This resulted in a out-of-bounds net_buf_push in hci_ipc.

This commit also enables asserts in hci_ipc in the audio bsim test, which reveal the out-of-bounds write.

Fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/82856

issue_context.title: Bluetooth: Controller: Out-of-bounds due to replaced net_buf reservation
issue_context.body:
`hci_ipc` in combination with the Zephyr Controller driver perform an out-of-bounds write.

#### Reproducing

Reproduces on `main` revision 8f07784e9fff4f5db5ba18a6e0be168cc4f70530

```bash
echo CONFIG_ASSERT=y >> "$ZEPHYR_BASE"/samples/bluetooth/hci_ipc/nrf5340_cpunet_iso-bt_ll_sw_split.conf
BOARD=nrf5340bsim/nrf5340/cpuapp "$ZEPHYR_BASE"/tests/bsim/bluetooth/audio/compile.sh
BOARD=nrf5340bsim/nrf5340/cpuapp "$ZEPHYR_BASE"/tests/bsim/bluetooth/audio/test_scripts/cap_broadcast_ac_13.sh
```

When the above steps are followed, an assertion is triggered in `hci_ipc` when `hci_ipc` is about to perform the out-of-bounds write. Assertions are off by default, so the out-of-bounds write actually happens by default in that test.

#### Cause

The underlying cause is the Controller driver replacing the reservation made by `hci_raw` for use by `hci_ipc`, here:

https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/8f07784e9fff4f5db5ba18a6e0be168cc4f70530/subsys/bluetooth/controller/hci/hci_driver.c#L162

#### Impact

The out-of-bounds write (and subsequent read) is at the end the adjacent buffer. There is potential for data corruption.

review_comments: Is it correct to have called `net_buf_reserve()` again after it has already been called in `bt_buf_get_rx()` and a type value assigned?
`net_buf_reserve` overwrites any previous reserved memory. Perhaps we need a `net_buf_add_reserve`?

Indeed. There isn't an API to increase reserved space, only set it. 

> Do you have a preference?

Of the two, I definitely prefer the former. Using `net_buf_pull` to increase reserved size seems way off :D 

There's also my suggestion with `net_buf_add_reserve` (or `net_buf_reserve_add`) we can suggest as a new API for net bufs. I wonder if there are other users doing the same

I experimented with the later, and see that the former option,i.e. the current use of `net_buf_reserve`  is functionally the least change required to fix the issue at hand. Approving this PR, and any improvement can be taken outside this PR.
